description: Equipo conformado por estudiantes de carreras STEM, creamos soluciones fuera de este planeta 😝
summary: HYDRUS 2040 is a video game anyone can play, with no prior knowledge required. It opens with short slides that set the context of the mission. Players then choose a planet, enter the number of players and their names, and equip their rocket, where every element has a role: weight, budget, power and more. Once they reach their destination, they must complete five objectives to pass the level. The game addresses the challenge by using real data to simulate a complete space mission, forcing players to make decisions about limited resources. It is important because it shows how a space mission is planned and built, while players discover real facts about each planet, such as gravity, sunlight and signal strength. Students and curious beginners build decision-making skills under constraints and learn that space science is accessible to everyone, all through play.
details:
HYDRUS 2040 is a browser based space mission game that needs no prior knowledge. After a comic-style intro narrated by Control Hydrus, players choose a destination (Mars, the Moon or Europa), then equip their rocket in the hangar. They set the fuel load, load equipment and assign crew stations while live meters track budget, weight, power and data. After launch, they reach the destination, complete five objectives and handle emergencies. Benefits: players learn how missions are designed by making the decisions themselves. They see that more weight means less Δv and that every choice has a cost.

They also pick up facts about each world, such as gravity, sunlight and signal. Impact: to make space science accessible and engaging for students and beginners, and to build decision-making under constraints. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SVG, plus. Creativity: one theme, “Follow the water,” runs across three worlds, Control Hydrus acts as a character, and the rocket builder shows trade-offs visually. Factors considered: accessibility (guided tour, skippable intro, keyboard controls), realism (real constraints and data), and replayability across three destinations.
